extraction.name: SWE-rebench
extraction.description: A public dataset of interactive Python-based software engineering tasks mined automatically from real-world GitHub repositories. It is designed to train and benchmark software engineering agents in diverse executable environments, including reinforcement learning settings.
extraction.creator: Ibragim Badertdinov, Alexander Golubev, Maksim Nekrashevich, Anton Shevtsov, Simon Karasik, Andrei Andriushchenko, Maria Trofimova, Daria Litvintseva, Boris Yangel
extraction.publisher: NeurIPS 2025 Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
extraction.rai:dataCollection: A fully automated four-stage pipeline continuously mined verifiable software engineering tasks from real-world GitHub repositories by downloading GitHub Archive issue/PR event data and cloning GitHub repositories, then filtering issue-linked merged PRs, automatically generating installation instructions, verifying tasks by executing tests in containers, and assessing task quality.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw/source data consisted of GitHub Archive daily JSON archives of public GitHub events and cloned GitHub repositories with full commit histories, including issue descriptions, discussions, linked pull requests, metadata, pull request merge status, commits, and discussions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Issues created before May 1, 2025; GitHub Archive accessed 15 May 2025.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Automated task quality assessment using an LLM fine-tuned on human annotations from SWE-bench Verified to predict three labels: Test Patch Correctness, Task Complexity, and Issue Clarity.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Validation of the automated annotation model on a validation set with classification metrics including precision, recall, F1, and accuracy; the paper also notes the approach was validated on a limited set of 18 repositories for prompt engineering.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct, including a fine-tuned version, was used for automated task quality assessment and label prediction; Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct was also used for LLM-driven generation of installation instructions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is biased toward Python open-source repositories with permissive licenses and tasks that can be automatically verified, which may limit representativeness. The automated pipeline also relies on heuristics and LLM judgments that can introduce errors.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The fully automated pipeline trades off manual curation for scalability, so some tasks may be imperfectly described, unsolvable from the issue alone, or lower quality due to errors in automated assessment. The installation-instruction method was validated on only 18 repositories, and the initial release is limited to Python, reducing applicability to other language ecosystems.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to improve transparency, standardization, openness, and responsible advancement in SWE-agent evaluation, but it may also accelerate increasingly autonomous software-engineering AI, with risks such as overreliance on AI-generated code and misuse for introducing vulnerabilities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for training and benchmarking/evaluating LLM-based software engineering agents, especially reinforcement-learning-based approaches, with metadata labels that let users filter tasks by clarity, complexity, and test correctness for model training or evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset/benchmark follows a continuous update plan: the pipeline is designed for continuous collection of fresh tasks, the public leaderboard is continuously updated, and future work includes keeping the benchmark up to date by maintaining evaluation on fresh tasks, evaluating more models, and sharing analyses.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The benchmark subset is curated from the larger dataset by applying filtering criteria; tasks can also be optionally filtered based on detected AttributeError/ImportError cases.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Dataset construction includes generating patches by diffing head_commit against base_commit (falling back to merge_commit if needed), generating test directives while filtering out deleted files, running tests with full error output to identify problematic AttributeError/ImportError cases, and freezing/recording dependency versions for reproducible environment setup.
